app.lema: Health monitoring for astronauts on missions

datalake.uso:
Usage:
  python index.py ingest goes|donki|radlab|eda [key=value ...]
  python index.py read <source> [from] [to]
  python index.py manifest
Language: VIGIA_LANG=es|en (default es)

app.name: VIGÍA
app.disclaimer: Decision-support prototype. Not a medical device. Thresholds are prototype rules with cited sources, not clinically validated flight limits. Environmental data labeled “Real” are NASA and NOAA measurements; in demo mode crew physiology is simulated.

about.lead: Halfway to Mars a message to the flight surgeon takes up to 22 minutes each way and evacuation is not possible. VIGÍA lets each astronaut evaluate their own health and decide the next step on board, without waiting for Earth.
about.challenge: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 · Challenge “Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions”
about.howLead: Three questions about each check-in, from the most urgent to the most subtle, with the environment as context.

log.d: Heart rate, blood pressure, SpO₂, temperature, sleep, mood and symptoms, in under 90 seconds.

compare.d: Against clinical limits, your own baseline and the measured environment.

act.d: Green, amber or red status, the reason and the next step.

layerQ.A: Is any value in the danger zone?
layerQ.C: Are you changing little by little?

layerHow.A: NEWS2 per-parameter bands (Royal College of Physicians), a terrestrial standard, with our own aggregation cut-offs, more conservative than the RCP triggers: red on an extreme band or a total of 5 or more; amber on 3 or 4. Prototype rules pending review by a flight surgeon.
layerHow.B: Compares each reading with your own baseline using a modified z-score (median and MAD, a robust measure of how much you usually vary). It alerts when it happens two days in a row.
layerHow.C: Adds up each day's small changes (one-sided CUSUM) to reveal a trend no single day shows. Active from day 21.
layerHow.context: A headache with cabin CO₂ above 3 mmHg is an environment alert for the crew, not a medical alert. A solar particle event switches on storm mode.

about.baseline: The baseline moves from pre-flight to in-flight: days 1–14 adaptation, 15–20 blend and, from day 21, an in-flight window with a 3-day lag.
about.dataLead: Every environmental value shows whether it is Real or Simulated, its source and its real date.
about.realPhys: Only what the crew member enters or the watch measures. Nothing is simulated.
about.realEnv: Measurements: GOES proton flux (NOAA SWPC) and DONKI solar particle events (NASA CCMC) on their real dates; RadLab dose (ALTEA-Survey, ISS) and EDA cabin CO₂, temperature and humidity (Rodent Research-1, ISS) re-anchored to the mission timeline.
about.demoPhys: A simulated 30-day crew member with three injected anomalies: slow drift, CO₂ spike with headache and a 200 pfu storm. Labeled “Simulated”.
about.demoEnv: The same real measurements, plus the injected anomalies labeled “Simulated”.
about.scenarioNote: Series from different years are placed on one mission timeline by an explicit scenario; the app never presents that coincidence as an observed fact.
about.privacyLead: Privacy is the rule; crew safety is the bounded exception.
about.privacyGreenBody: Never leave the device. After 3 days in amber, VIGÍA recommends sharing it.
about.privacyRedBody: Escalated automatically to the crew medical officer with the minimum data: indicator, value, time and band. The astronaut sees exactly what was sent.
about.offlineBody: The app shell, the engine, the check-in and the alerts run with the network off; check-ins and escalations queue locally and sync when the link returns. Reports to the ground travel through a delay queue.
about.resultsLead: 500 simulated missions with anomalies and 500 control missions (seed 2026). Not clinical performance.

drift.l: Slow drift detected (sleep −0.2 h/day, HR +1 bpm/day, mood −0.15/day), median 8 days after onset

half.l: The same drift at half intensity

fixed.l: A fixed terrestrial threshold (HR ≥ 91 bpm) fired

rules.l: CO₂ + headache and solar storm rules (deterministic)

false.l: False alarms per crew member per week

about.resultsCaveat: These numbers are optimistic: the simulated noise is Gaussian and the generator was written by the same team. They show that the engine sees a drift that a fixed threshold misses, not how it would perform on real crews.

limitsList.phys: Crew physiology in demo mode is simulated; no real astronaut data is used. Clinical bands come from NEWS2, a terrestrial standard, and the aggregation cut-offs are ours; both need review by a flight surgeon.
limitsList.rad: Radiation is ambient dose from an area detector, not personal dose. GOES measures at geostationary orbit: it indicates severity and timing, not crew dose.
limitsList.todo: Not yet implemented: body mass in layer C, the in-flight metrology correction of layer A, the PVT-B vigilance test, camera input, storage encryption and crew authentication.

about.sourcesNote: Full references are in the technical report of the repository.
about.aiBody: We used AI assistants (Claude, by Anthropic, through Claude Code; OpenAI Codex as an independent reviewer) to research public NASA, CSA and NOAA sources, to draft and review documentation and to help write, review and test code. Decisions, indicators, rules and sources are the team's. No AI-generated images, video or audio.
about.provMeasured: Entered by the astronaut or streamed from a paired device.
about.provSimulated: Synthetic physiology and injected anomalies from demo mode.
about.provScenario: Mission calendar: the day on which each real window falls is a scenario decision.
about.provReal: Public NASA and NOAA measurements re-anchored to mission days, with their real date.

0.1: Dose and solar particle events from space weather.

2.1: Communication delay; the crew must act first.

3.1: Fluid shift, bone and muscle loss, vision changes.

4.1: CO2, temperature, humidity and cabin pressure.

about.title: About VIGÍA
about.earthLead: The same pattern serves wherever the doctor is far away and evacuation is not immediate: a daily self-assessment against your own baseline, with the environment as context.

0.1: One doctor for the crew and nine months of winter with no possible evacuation; ESA uses it as an analog for long-duration missions. VIGÍA would give each person their status and next step before consulting.

1.1: CSA explores bringing Bio-Monitor wearable monitoring to regions far from a hospital. A daily check-in with a personal baseline changes the decision of when to ask for a transfer.

trayecto.title: Trajectory to Mars
trayecto.label: Trajectory to Mars, day {dia}: the ship is {dist} from Earth and the communication delay is {retardo}
trayecto.help: The ship follows a Hohmann transfer orbit: it leaves Earth and reaches Mars after 259 days. Each mission day has a position, which gives the communication delay and the accumulated dose. It is a simulated scenario, not real ephemerides.
trayecto.doseNote: Scenario model: background radiation of about 1.8 mSv per day plus solar storms. Not a measurement.

banda.A: NEWS2 band total of 5 or more, or one parameter in its extreme range (VIGÍA cut-off)
banda.B: Outside your personal band two days in a row
banda.C: Cumulative drift over several days (CUSUM of 5 or more)

MOTOR.bandaAAmbar: NEWS2 band total of 3 or 4 (VIGÍA cut-off)

bandaContexto.co2: CO2 above 3 mmHg (1 h average) with headache
bandaContexto.protones: Flux of 10 pfu or more at ≥10 MeV, or SEP event

causa.A: A reading crosses a clinical safety limit.
causa.B: The reading departs from your current personal baseline.
causa.C: A sustained drift from your in-flight baseline has been building up over several days.
causa.context: The measured environment explains the symptom or calls for action by the whole crew.

causaContexto.co2: You reported a headache and cabin CO2 exceeds the limit: the likely cause is environmental, not medical.
causaContexto.protones: A solar particle event is in progress: storm mode is activated for the whole crew.

accion.fc: Sit down for 5 minutes without talking and take your pulse again. If it is still above 100 bpm at rest, or it is high again tomorrow when you wake up, share it today with the Crew Medical Officer.
accion.pas: Sit with your back supported, rest for 5 minutes and take your blood pressure again. If the first number is still 140 or higher, or you notice a headache or blurred vision, tell the Crew Medical Officer today.
accion.sueno: Tonight, turn off screens 1 hour before bed and set aside 8 hours in a row for sleep. Log how long you slept tomorrow: if you sleep less than 6 hours for a third night, or you feel drowsy during critical tasks, mention it to the Crew Medical Officer.
accion.animo: Today, set aside 30 minutes to talk with a crewmate or your family and do something you enjoy. Log your mood again tomorrow: if it stays low for 3 days in a row, or you find it hard to sleep, eat or concentrate, mention it to the Crew Medical Officer.
accion.news2: Sit down now, do not stay alone and find the Crew Medical Officer right away. Repeat the measurements in 5 minutes with them at your side, even if you already feel better.
accion.co2: Turn up the ventilation or check the CO2 scrubber and move closer to an air outlet. Repeat the check-in in 30 minutes: if the headache continues, or dizziness or shortness of breath appear, alert the whole crew to check the cabin air.
accion.protones: Alert the whole crew and go to the shielded area now; stay there until the solar storm warning ends. If in the next few hours you notice nausea, vomiting or heavy tiredness, tell the Crew Medical Officer; today's readings are flagged because of the storm.
accion.glucosa: Wash your hands and repeat the measurement with a new strip (the used one goes in the biological waste container). If it reads below 70, have something sugary and measure again in 15 minutes; if it reads above 126 while fasting, drink water and measure again tomorrow before breakfast. If it is out of that range again, tell the Crew Medical Officer today.

MOTOR.estable: All readings within your baseline band and safety limits.
MOTOR.sinDatos: No readings for this day yet. Complete your check-in to evaluate it.

zona.head: Carry on with today's routine. If you notice blurred vision, a headache or dizziness, note it in today's check-in; if it happens two days in a row, mention it to the Crew Medical Officer.
zona.heart: Complete today's exercise session and drink at least 2 liters of water. Take your pulse tomorrow when you wake up, before getting up: if it is over 100 bpm, or you notice palpitations or shortness of breath, note it in the check-in and mention it to the Crew Medical Officer.
zona.bone: Complete today's strength exercise session. If during or after the session you notice pain in your back, hips or heels, note it in the check-in; if it lasts more than 2 days, mention it to the Crew Medical Officer.
zona.blood: Wash your hands before eating and take your temperature tomorrow when you wake up. If it reaches 38 °C, or you notice a sore throat or unusual tiredness, note it in the check-in and tell the Crew Medical Officer.
zona.mind: Tonight, turn off screens 1 hour before bed and set aside 8 hours for sleep. Log tomorrow how long you slept and how you feel: if you sleep less than 6 hours or your mood drops two days in a row, mention it to the Crew Medical Officer.

MOTOR.bandaSintoma: Symptom with no measured environmental cause
MOTOR.causaSintoma: You reported a symptom and the measured environment (cabin CO2) does not explain it.

accionSintoma.head: Rest, drink water and stay off screens for 1 hour. Log the symptom again in 2 hours: if it is still the same tomorrow, or sooner if your vision blurs, you get dizzy when moving or the pain is the worst you remember, find the Crew Medical Officer.
accionSintoma.blood: Take your temperature now, wash your hands well and do not share cutlery or towels. Take it again tomorrow morning and at night: if it reaches 38 °C, or the symptom is still there the day after tomorrow, tell the Crew Medical Officer.
